avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce hepatic metabolism and reduce levetiracetam levels; also has seizure-lowering threshold potential
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if patient already taking, do not abruptly discontinue without consulting prescriber

avoid_supplements.name: Evening Primrose Oil
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May lower seizure threshold and reduce antiepileptic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use only under close medical supervision

caution_supplements.name: Ginkgo Biloba
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential additive CNS effects and theoretical seizure threshold reduction
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased dizziness, somnolence, or lack of seizure control

caution_supplements.name: Valerian Root
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additive CNS depression may increase sedation and dizziness
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for enhanced drowsiness or impaired cognition

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS depression may increase somnolence, dizziness, and cognitive impairment
caution_foods.action: Minimize or avoid alcohol consumption; counsel on impaired coordination and judgment

monitoring_notes: Levetiracetam undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism with predominant renal excretion, resulting in few clinically significant drug-nutrient interactions. Primary monitoring should focus on CNS adverse effects and seizure control, with renal function assessment in patients with impaired kidney function.
